validity.researcher_notes: The line is real and correctly classified as a transmission gas trunk. Ukrtransgaz's history page, the Kursk regional government page, Gazprom's Yelets pipeline division page and Ukrainian Wikipedia all name it. It is not a duplicate of P0776: Ukrtransgaz lists the Kyiv line (1982) and the Dykanka line (1984) separately, the VTG table lists them with different lengths (478 and 507 km), and the routes-repo geometry splits at Kursk. It is also not P0783 or P1460, which are a larger-diameter line and a consecutive line meeting at Dykanka. Problem: the sheet length of 298 km has no source, and the VTG design-institute table gives 478 km. The owner share of 48.60% for Gazprom has no source. The end district Dykanka Raion no longer exists since 2020.

fills.researcher_notes: No source dated 2024 or later was found that says this line is in use. The Kursk regional government page (archived December 2022) and the Gazprom Kursk compressor-station page (archived May 2025) both list the line, but only as part of the corridor's history. Russian transit through Ukraine stopped on 1 January 2025. Searched Russian and Ukrainian news, the Ukrainian operator site is blocked (HTTP 403).
